\[
g_C = \frac{1}{P_{ 99 }(C)},
\quad
C' = \begin{cases} \operatorname{srgb}\left(g_C \operatorname{lin}(C)\right) & \text{linear light} \\ g_C\, C & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(P_p(C)\): The p-th percentile of channel C, as a fraction of white
- \(g_C\): The gain of channel C

P_p(C) is the p-th percentile of channel C, as a fraction of white, in linear light if it is on. It uses the linear rule of numpy.percentile on the levels 0 to 255 of the whole image. The white-patch assumption, from the retinex work of Land and McCann, is that the brightest surface in a scene is white, so its color is the color of the light. The gains bring that color to white. Percentile 100 is the max-RGB method, and lower percentiles keep a few bright or noisy pixels from setting the gains. With Linear light on, the default, the gains act on linear light values: decoded from sRGB, scaled, and encoded again. A change in the color of the light scales linear values, so this is the physical model. With it off, the gains scale the encoded values. A channel whose percentile is 0 gets gain 1.
